title: The Karnaugh Map: Gray-Code Cells, Numbering and Wrap-Around
quickIdea: A K-map is a truth table folded into a grid so that logically adjacent rows - rows differing in one bit - are physically adjacent cells; the row and column labels must therefore be in Gray code.
remember: An n-variable map has 2^n cells, one per minterm. Rows and columns are labelled in the order 00, 01, 11, 10, not 00, 01, 10, 11, so that neighbours differ in exactly one bit.

Four-variable numbering with rows AB and columns CD both in Gray order: 0, 1, 3, 2 in the first row; 4, 5, 7, 6 in the second; 12, 13, 15, 14 in the third; 8, 9, 11, 10 in the fourth. The 3 sits before the 2 - that swap is the whole method.
The map is a torus: the left and right edges are adjacent, the top and bottom edges are adjacent, and the four corners are mutually adjacent, so m0, m2, m8 and m10 form a legal group of four.
Each cell has exactly n neighbours: 2 in a two-variable map, 3 in a three-variable map, 4 in a four-variable map, and 5 in a five-variable map.
A cell holds a 1, a 0 or an X for a don't care; the grid is only a picture of the truth table and carries no new information.

A three-variable map is a 2-by-4 grid with rows AB in Gray order and columns C = 0, 1, or its transpose; either convention groups identically, but the numbering must be read from the labels, never from the position.

example.prompt: In a four-variable map, list the cells adjacent to m0, and say what the group {m0, m2, m8, m10} simplifies to.
example.work: m0 is 0000. Its four neighbours are m1 = 0001, m2 = 0010, m4 = 0100 and m8 = 1000. Wrap-around makes m2 the top-bottom neighbour and m8 the left-right neighbour, and the corner m10 = 1010 is adjacent to m2 and to m8, so all four corners are one group. In the four corners A and C take every combination while B and D stay 0, so the term keeps B' and D' and drops A and C.
example.answer: m0's neighbours are m1, m2, m4 and m8; the group of four corners is B'D'.

gateAngle: Every map question begins with numbering, and a mis-numbered cell is the commonest way to lose the marks. GATE CSE 1998 Q.2.7 is the exception that proves the rule: its printed map was not in Gray order, so the accepted solution converts it to standard form before grouping.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: GATE CSE 1998 Q.2.7: The function represented by the given Karnaugh map is (A) A.B (B) AB + BC + CA (C) NOT(B XOR C) (D) A.BC
variations.answer: Option (C), that is B XNOR C.
variations.why: The map as printed changes two variables between consecutive columns, which makes merging unsafe; converted to Gray order it groups to BC + B'C' = B XNOR C. The lesson is to check the labels before drawing any group.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: How many cells has a five-variable map, and how many neighbours has each cell?
variations.why: 2^5 = 32, and a cell is adjacent to the cell that differs in each of the five variables - one neighbour per variable. In a four-variable map the same count is 4, which is why a corner cell in a 4-by-4 map has four neighbours even though it looks like it has two.

trap.what: Numbering the cells in binary order, or assuming only the drawn edges are adjacent.
trap.why: Binary order puts 2 and 3 in the wrong columns, so a pair that differs in one bit stops being adjacent and a pair that differs in two bits starts to look adjacent. And the wrap-around edges are as real as the drawn ones.
trap.counterexample: In binary order the cells of a quad would read 0, 1, 2, 3, whose corner pair 0 and 3 differs in two bits; in Gray order the same four cells are 0, 1, 3, 2 and each neighbour pair differs in one bit.

check.question: Which minterms are adjacent to m5 in a four-variable map, and what is the group {m5, m7} as a product term?
check.answer: m5 is adjacent to m4 (0100), m7 (0111), m13 (1101) and m1 (0001); the group {m5, m7} is A'BD.
check.explanation: m5 = 0101. The four neighbours flip one bit each: 0100, 0111, 1101 and 0001. m5 and m7 both have A = 0, B = 1, D = 1 and differ only in C, so C drops and the term is A'BD.

sources.note: read from the opening to the two-variable map and its minterm numbering, plus the closing summary: the truth table rewritten as a grid, the A/B axis reading, the minterm numbering m0..m3, the first grouping (AB' + AB = A), and the summary's four rules - logical adjacency is the whole method, SOP covers every 1 with the fewest and largest power-of-two groups, POS covers the 0s, and a don't care is treated as 0 or 1 according to which makes the group larger. The middle of the transcript was not served, so the 3- and 4-variable worked examples are not attributed to it.

sources.title: Karnaugh map: Gray-code ordering, grouping and wrap-around
sources.note: read the construction and grouping sections: the grid ordered in Gray code so that adjacent cells differ in one variable, groups rectangular with an area a power of two, groups allowed to overlap, toroidal connectivity so that the extreme right column is adjacent to the far left and the top row to the bottom, and the rule for reading a term by keeping the variables that do not change across the box.
